All the days (all the time) of his life he lived in the abundance of wealth and the honor that comes from kings.
It is said
that when he was dying, his son said to him:
"What is causing you pain?" And he replied:
"This quantity of ninety years."
And again he asked him:
"What do you desire?" And he replied:
"To desire."
And in the year 1476
[1476 of the Greeks / 1165 AD], we heard a wondrous tale from the inhabitants of the village of Alynas {Alinas}:
that when there was a pestilence in that year in Cyrrhus {Grophya?}:
A certain Turk came up to them and said to them:
"Find out who died first in this pestilence." And when they found out,
they opened his grave and found him, after four months, with his body not decayed,
and his eyes wide open,
and his mouth open about a span and four fingers,
and the part of the shroud covering his head and his chest was eaten,
and his beard, which was around his face, was trimmed as if with shears,
and his right arm had come down from its shoulder-joint onto his side.
Then that Turk closed his mouth
and drove a large stake into it.
And no one else died from that day on.
And in the year 1477
[1477 of the Greeks / 1166 AD], Manuel, the king of the Greeks,
in a battle with the Bulgarians,
was struck and fell from his horse.
And when a Bulgarian stood over him to kill him,
he made known to him that he was the king,
and he promised great bounties to the one who captured him,
with solemn oaths,
if he would bring him to Constantinople.
And the Bulgarian believed him,
and brought him to the city.
And the king fulfilled his promise,
and gave more besides.
And it is said
that at that time,
that Manuel, concerning the queen,
because she was not bearing children,
deceitfully killed her with poison,
and a second wife,
which is not lawful for kings (for a king),
he took.
And in the year 1478
[1478] of the Greeks (1167 of our Lord),
which is 562
of the Arabs,
for a second time Nur al-Din sent the emir Asad al-Din Shirkuh and Salah al-Din, his nephew, to Egypt.
And because that Shirkuh was eager and longing for this,
with swift marches he reached Egypt,
and crossed the River Nile to the western side,
and spread out as far as the country of Sa'id {Upper Egypt}.
